abstract: Research and development (R&D) can propel enterprise development and long-term competitiveness. This study provides a cultural explanation for enterprises’ R&D activities through causal evidence. Using data from 36,024 firm-year observations of Chinese listed companies from 2010 to 2022, this study applies machine learning methods to measure corporate culture and finds that stronger corporate culture significantly increases firms’ engagement in R&D activities. We find that stronger corporate culture increases the R&D expenditures and enhances R&D intensity. A one SD increase in corporate culture strength leads to a 15% increase in R&D expenditure. This indicates that enterprises with stronger cultures are better able to obtain external resources and strengthen internal governance. Heterogeneity analysis illustrates that the impact of corporate culture is more evident among non-state-owned enterprises (non-SOEs), non-manufacturing enterprises, enterprises that adopt digital technologies, and those with low resilience, low market attention and high uncertainty. This pattern suggests that corporate culture provides greater strategic significance to enterprises with limited resources or those traversing complex external environments, thus augmenting technology adoption. The findings provide innovative insights into how informal institutions can encourage innovation in emerging economies.
